messages:
elaine: Quick ask — we need a small 'stat pack' for launch copy and a reproducible artifact set. Specifically: p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end latency, separate warm vs cold starts, and traces for 2k sample requests. Two model variants: redwood-7b-v1 (float16) and int8-quantized. Hosted API only. Can you confirm feasibility and ETA? :eyes:

matt: @elaine we can do that. To confirm: you want full-percentile aggregation for 10k requests, plus 2k traced requests? Also do you need batch sizes tested?

elaine: Exactly — marketing wants aggregated percentiles over 10k samples for each variant, plus 2k full traces (call + kernel timings). Test batch sizes 1 and 8. Keep input profile at ~256 tokens. Also include the raw payloads and a tiny harness so the claims are reproducible. Need by Tue EOD for press review.

sam: For the quantized run we should pin the kernel selection and the compilation tag. Also clarity on sampling: do you want uniform sampling from our corpus or seeded synthetic prompts?

elaine: Uniform sampling from our anonymized demo corpus is fine, but we need the seed and sampling code included. Determinism is important for audit.

matt: Understood. A couple of operational notes: 10k full traces is heavy on storage. Proposal: provide aggregated metrics for 10k, and upload 2k full trace artifacts. We'll include the sampled 10k payload list (no traces) plus the 2k raw traces. Also include warmup procedure and the exact docker/container tag. ETA: Tue 10:00 PT if we start tomorrow morning. Is that acceptable?

dina: That works for legal/PR. Please make warm vs cold explicit in results and include the short README describing the reproduction steps. We also need a short statement of the test harness config (batching, concurrency, HW).

matt: Plan: run both variants (float16, int8) with batch sizes [1,8], run a warmup of 500 requests, then the 10k sample sweep. We'll capture end-to-end latencies and also the kernel-level timings for the 2k subset. Will pin runtime version and kernel tag in the README. I can also attach a minimal `curl` example and a tiny harness script.

elaine: For the headline, marketing hopes p95 < 250ms for float16 and p95 <= 350ms for int8 (same batch). Don't overfit — we want representative numbers. If runs deviate a lot, call it out in a note.

matt: Noted — we'll run a first pass and surface any instability. One question: streaming latency vs end-to-end completion latency — which should be primary?

elaine: Primary: end-to-end. Include streaming metrics as secondary if easy.

runtime-bot: runner: started bench job job-48291 for job-config runtime/statpack/175303 at 1753038000

matt: Logging job job-48291. I'll post artifacts (S3 link) and a short README when complete. @elaine will ping when uploaded.

elaine: Great — thanks team :thumbsup:
